enonce.question:
Rayen wants to send an email to his cousin Malek to tell him about his holidays in Tabarka.

1) Choose the two greetings that suit an informal email: Dear Sir, / Hi Malek, / Hello Malek, / Dear Mr Trabelsi,
2) Complete the rule: an informal email begins with Hi or Hello + the person's ______ name.
3) Choose the suitable first sentence after the greeting: How are you? I hope you are well. / I am writing to inform you of my arrival.
4) Write the greeting of an email to your best friend.

Yasmine wants to write an email to the headmaster of her school, Mr Chebbi, to ask for information about the science club.

1) Choose the correct greeting for this formal email: Hi Chebbi! / Dear Mr Chebbi, / Hello friend,
2) Yasmine also writes to a language centre, but she does not know the director's name. Choose her greeting: Dear Sir or Madam, / Hey there,
3) Complete the rule: a formal email begins with ______ + Mr / Mrs / Ms + family name.
4) Choose the suitable first sentence: Guess what! / I am writing to ask for information about the science club.

Read Ahmed's email. The subject line is empty.
Subject: ______
Dear Mrs Mabrouk,
I am writing to tell you that I will be absent on Monday because I have a medical appointment. I will copy the lessons from my classmate.
Yours sincerely,
Ahmed Ferjani

1) What do we write in the subject line?
2) Choose the best subject: a) Hello — b) Absence on Monday — c) I will be absent on Monday because I have a medical appointment
3) Why are the two others not good?
4) Write a subject line for an email inviting a friend to a football match.

Read Wiem's formal email. She forgot the capital letters and the punctuation.
dear sir I want to inform you that the school trip is on friday
i will send you the programme tomorrow
yours faithfully
wiem ben amor

1) Rewrite the greeting correctly (capital letters and punctuation mark).
2) Rewrite the two sentences of the body with capital letters and full stops.
3) Rewrite the closing and the name correctly.
4) Complete the rule: after the greeting and after the closing, we put a ______.

Read Emna's email to the director of a summer camp.
Dear Mr Haddad,
I am writing to ask for information about your summer camp in Hammamet. Could you please send me the dates and the prices? I look forward to your reply.
______
Emna Sassi

1) Choose the two closings that suit this formal email: Yours sincerely, / Lots of love, / Best regards, / See you!
2) Why are the two others wrong here?
3) When an email begins with “Dear Sir or Madam,”, which closing do we use: Yours faithfully, or Bye for now,?
4) What does Emna write under the closing?

Read this email.
Dear Mrs Jebali,
I am writing to say that I cannot come to the English club tomorrow because I have a doctor's appointment. I am sorry, as I really enjoy the club.
Best regards,
Seif

1) Find the two linking words that introduce a reason.
2) Join the two sentences with because: I was late. I missed the bus.
3) Choose the right connector: I stayed at home (because / so / but) I was ill.
4) Complete with your own reason: I like English because ______.

Here are the four parts of Lina's email, in the wrong order.
a) See you soon, Lina
b) Hi Mariem,
c) I am writing to invite you to my birthday party on Saturday at four o'clock. We are going to eat cake and play games.
d) Subject: Birthday party invitation

1) Name each part: greeting, body, closing or subject.
2) Put the four parts in the correct order.
3) Which part does the reader see first, before opening the email?
4) Which part gives the reason for writing?

Read Aymen's email to his friend. The closing is missing.
Hi Skander,
How are you? I hope you are well. I am writing to tell you about my new school. It is big and the teachers are nice. Please write back soon!
______
Aymen

1) Choose the two closings that suit this informal email: Yours faithfully, / See you soon, / Best wishes, / Yours sincerely,
2) Why are the two other closings not suitable here?
3) Give one more informal closing.
4) Which punctuation mark follows the closing?

Read these phrases from different emails.
a) Hey, wanna hang out?
b) I would like to invite you to our school open day.
c) Thanks a lot for the pics!
d) I would be grateful if you could send me the timetable.

1) Say if each phrase is formal or informal.
2) Which words in a) and c) show the style? Give their standard forms.
3) Rewrite a) in a more formal way.
4) Who can you send phrase a) to: a friend or the headmaster?
Write the opening line of an email inviting a friend.
What is the structure of the first conditional?
Complete: If it rains, we ___ (stay) at home.
Complete: If you ___ (study), you will pass.
Complete: If we recycle, we ___ (protect) the environment.

Ons wants to invite her classmates to a picnic. Read what she says. There is a mistake in each sentence.
a) If I will see him, I will tell him.
b) If Rami will come, he will bring his guitar.
c) We will have a great time if the weather will be nice.

1) Find the mistake in each if-clause.
2) Rewrite the three sentences correctly.
3) Complete the rule: If + ______ simple, ... will + base verb. We never use ______ in the if-clause.
Complete: She won't come if you ___ (not / invite) her.

Nour is talking to her little brother about their afternoon. Read her notes.
| Condition | Result |
|---|---|
| I have time | I will help you |
| you finish your homework | we will go to the park |
| it rains | we will stay at home |

1) Join the first line with if. Begin with: If I have time, ...
2) Join the two other lines in the same way.
3) Which tense comes after if? Which form is in the result clause?
4) Where do we put the comma?

Read the teacher's advice before the ninth-year exam.
If you revise a little every day, you will remember your lessons. If you sleep well before the exam, you will not feel tired. You will get good marks if you read the questions carefully.

1) Find the verbs in the three if-clauses. Which tense are they in?
2) Which form is used in the result clauses?
3) Use the notes to write a first conditional sentence: (I / study hard) → (I / pass the exam).
4) Write two first conditional sentences of your own about studying: one with If at the beginning and one with if in the middle.
Use "unless": ___ you hurry, you will miss the bus.

Compare the two sentences.
A. If it rains, we will stay at home.
B. We will stay at home if it rains.

1) Do sentences A and B have the same meaning? Can the if-clause come second?
2) Which sentence has a comma? Complete the rule: we use a comma only when the if-clause comes ______.
3) Rewrite with the if-clause second: If you hurry, you will catch the bus.
4) Rewrite with the if-clause first: She will be happy if she wins the prize.
Comparative + than: A plane is ___ (fast) a car.

Read the information about three basketball players.
| Player | Height |
|---|---|
| Amir | $185\ \text{cm}$ |
| Wael | $192\ \text{cm}$ |
| Nizar | $178\ \text{cm}$ |

1) Write the superlative form of tall.
2) Complete with a name and a superlative: ______ is ______ player of the three.
3) Write the superlative of short, then write a sentence about Nizar.
4) Complete the rule: short adjective → the + adjective + ______.
Complete: This is ___ (interesting) book I have read.
Superlative of "good".
Superlative of "happy".

Samir compares the members of his family, but he makes one mistake in each sentence.
a) He is more taller than me.
b) My sister is more young than my brother.
c) My father is the most oldest in the family.

1) Find the mistake in each sentence.
2) Rewrite the three sentences correctly.
3) Complete the rule: we never use “more” or “most” together with ______ or ______.

Look at the prices in a phone shop.
| Phone | Price |
|---|---|
| Alpha | 450 dinars |
| Nova | 900 dinars |
| Star | 1600 dinars |

1) Write the superlative form of expensive.
2) Complete: The ______ is the ______ ______ phone in the shop.
3) Write a sentence about the Alpha with the superlative of cheap.
4) Why do we say “the most expensive” but “the cheapest”?

Read the information about two Tunisian cities.
| Fact | Tunis | Sfax |
|---|---|---|
| Size | the biggest city in the country | big, but smaller than Tunis |
| Position | north | centre-east |
| Known for | capital city | port, olive oil |

1) Write a sentence comparing the size of the two cities with bigger than.
2) Write the same idea beginning with Sfax and using not as ... as.
3) Complete with a superlative: Tunis is ______ (big) city in Tunisia.
4) Write two sentences of your own to compare places you know (one comparative and one superlative).
Complete: He is ___ (bad) player in the team.
Complete (equality): She is ___ tall ___ her brother.

Read the dialogue.
Maher: Where is Mr Baccar, the sports teacher?
Youssef: I ______ (saw / have seen) him yesterday in the gym.
Maher: And today?
Youssef: No, I ______ (didn't see / haven't seen) him today.

1) Choose the correct form in the first gap. Which word helps you?
2) Choose the correct form in the second gap. Is today finished?
3) Choose: She (visited / has visited) Tozeur last summer.
4) Give two other time expressions that go with the past simple.

Read about Mrs Lamia.
Mrs Lamia came to Mahdia in 2019 and she still lives there today. She started working at the hospital in 2020 and she still works there. She met her best friend, Samia, three years ago, and they are still friends.

1) Complete: She ______ (live) here since 2019.
2) Complete: She ______ (work) at the hospital since 2020.
3) Complete: Lamia and Samia ______ (be) friends for three years.
4) Why do we use the present perfect, and not the past simple, in these sentences?

Two friends talk about a new film at the cinema.
Sami: Is the new adventure film good?
Anas: I don't know. We ______ (not / see) that film yet. My sister ______ (already / buy) the tickets, but my father ______ (not / finish) his work yet.

1) Complete the dialogue with the present perfect.
2) Where do we put yet in the sentence? Is it used here in affirmative or negative sentences?
3) Where do we put already?
4) Write a negative sentence with yet about your homework.

Ms Brown, an English teacher, talks to her new Tunisian pupil.
Ms Brown: (you / ever / be) to London?
Hedi: No, I haven't. I have never been to England.
Ms Brown: (you / ever / visit) the Bardo Museum?
Hedi: Yes, I have.
Ms Brown: (your parents / ever / travel) by plane?
Hedi: Yes, they have.

1) Write Ms Brown's three questions in the present perfect.
2) Where do we put ever in the question?
3) Give the past participle of: be, visit, travel.

Read the note on the kitchen table.
Dear Mum, I ______ (go) to the library with Salma. Dad ______ (go) to the market. We ______ (take) the keys. See you at six! — Ines

1) Give the three forms of the verb go: base form, past simple, past participle.
2) Complete the note with the present perfect.
3) Complete the rule: present perfect = have / ______ + past ______.
4) Write the negative of: Dad has gone to the market.

Read about Mr Gharbi.
Mr Gharbi is a teacher of English in Gabès. He started teaching in 2010 and he is still a teacher today. He moved to his present house two years ago.

1) Complete with for or since: ______ two years / ______ 2010 / ______ Monday / ______ a long time.
2) Complete: He has lived in his house ______ two years.
3) Complete: He has taught English ______ 2010.
4) Complete the rule: ______ + a period of time; ______ + a starting point.
Choose: I ___ (already finished/have already finished) my work.
Explain when to use present perfect.
Which tense with "yesterday, last week, in 2010"?

Read Tarek's message. He makes three mistakes with the past simple and the present perfect.
Hi Bilel! Do you know Mr Smith, our new neighbour? (a) I have seen him last night. (b) He has arrived in Tunis two days ago. (c) I never spoke to an Englishman in my life, so I am a bit shy!

1) Find the time expressions in (a) and (b). Are they finished times?
2) Correct sentences (a) and (b).
3) Correct sentence (c). Which words tell you to use the present perfect?
4) Complete the rule: finished time (last night, ago) → ______; life experience with no exact time → ______.
Choose: Water ___ (boils/is boiling) at 100°C. (general truth)
Choose: Look! It ___ (snows/is snowing). (now)

It is evening in the Mejri family's flat.
Listen! Someone ______ (sing) in the bathroom. Look! The cat ______ (sleep) on the sofa. Right now, the children ______ (do) their homework.

1) Complete with the present continuous of the verbs in brackets.
2) Which words in the text tell you that the actions are happening now?
3) Choose the correct form: My father (sings / is singing) every morning.
4) Is “someone” followed by is or are?
Complete: I usually ___ (walk) to school, but today I ___ (take) the bus.
Complete: She ___ (work) in a bank. (permanent)
Time expression for simple vs continuous?

In the classroom, the teacher asks a question and three pupils speak. Each sentence has a mistake.
a) I am knowing the answer.
b) I am not understanding this word.
c) Sir, I am wanting some help, please.

1) Rewrite the three sentences correctly.
2) What kind of verbs are know, understand and want? Can we use them in the present continuous?
3) Choose the correct form: Look! Ahmed (writes / is writing) on the board. He (likes / is liking) English.
Complete: They ___ (build) a new house this month. (temporary)
Explain the difference in one sentence.
Which verbs are not used in continuous? (state verbs)

Read about the Karray family.
In the evening, everyone uses technology. Father reads the news on his laptop. Mother calls her sister with her smartphone. Little Adam watches cartoons on a tablet, and Grandfather listens to his old radio.

1) Find in the text three modern devices.
2) Say what each person does with his or her modern device.
3) Sort these words into technology / environment: smartphone, pollution, laptop, waste, tablet.
4) Name two modern devices that you or your family use.

Read the text.
In Amal's school, there are three bins: one for paper, one for plastic bottles and one for other rubbish. The pupils do not throw paper and plastic away. A factory takes them and makes new products: new paper and new bottles. The pupils recycle their waste.

1) What does “recycle” mean? Choose: a) to throw waste in the street — b) to use old materials to make new products — c) to buy new things.
2) Find in the text two materials that the pupils recycle.
3) Complete: We should ______ paper and plastic to protect the environment.
4) Give the noun: recycle → ______.
What is "pollution"?

Read the short text.
Many countries use oil, gas and coal to make electricity, but these fuels pollute the air and they will finish one day. Renewable energy is different: it comes from nature and it does not finish. In the south of Tunisia, the sun shines almost every day, and on the coast the wind is often strong.

1) Find in the text two natural things that can give renewable energy, and name the two sources of energy.
2) Sort these words into renewable / not renewable: oil, solar energy, coal, wind energy, gas.
3) Complete: Solar and wind power are clean, so they do not ______ the air.
Give one advantage of technology.

Read what Zied says about his tablet.
I use the internet every day. Yesterday I found a good dictionary app on a website. I downloaded it, and now the app is on my tablet. Then I uploaded my holiday photos to share them with my cousins.

1) What does “download” mean? Choose: a) to copy a file from the internet to your device — b) to send a file from your device to the internet — c) to switch off a device.
2) Which word in the text is the opposite of download?
3) What did Zied download? Where is it now?
4) Complete: You can ______ music, games and apps from the internet.
Complete: We should ___ energy to protect the planet.
Give one disadvantage of technology.
What is "global warming"?
Write a sentence about protecting the environment.
Choose: The man ___ lives here is my uncle. (who/which)
Choose: The book ___ I read was great. (who/which)
Join: The girl is my friend. She won the prize.
Which relative pronoun for possession?
Complete: That is the teacher ___ car is new. (whose)
Complete: The place ___ we met was a park. (where)
Which pronoun for time (day, year)?

Read Meriam's sentences. In each one there is an extra pronoun.
a) The car which is red it is mine.
b) The girl who lives next door she is my friend.
c) This is the book which I bought it yesterday.

1) Find the extra word in each sentence.
2) Rewrite the three sentences correctly.
3) Explain why the extra word is wrong.
4) Join the two sentences without making this mistake: The man is a doctor. He lives opposite the school.
Join with "who": I know a boy. He speaks five languages.

Hamdi shows his grandmother's village to a friend.
a) This is the house. I was born in it.
b) That is the school. My mother studied there.
c) This is the baker. He makes the best bread in the village.

1) Join the two sentences in a) with where.
2) Join the sentences in b) with where and the sentences in c) with who.
3) Which words disappear from the second sentence in a) and in b) when we use where?
4) Rewrite a) with which and the preposition in.
What happens to present simple in reported speech?
Report: "will" becomes ___.

Before leaving the youth club, three friends made promises to Ali.
Mourad said, “I will call you.”
Sana said, “I will bring my camera.”
The twins said, “We will come early.”

1) Ali reports Mourad's words later. Write his sentence. Begin with: He said (that) ...
2) Report Sana's words and the twins' words.
3) Complete the rule: in reported speech, will changes to ______.
4) Which pronoun replaces “you” in Mourad's sentence when Ali reports it?

Hiba reports what her classmates said yesterday, but she forgets to change the tense.
a) He said that he is happy.
b) She said that she has a new bike.
c) They said that they can swim.

1) What is the tense of the reporting verb “said”?
2) Rewrite the three sentences correctly.
3) Complete the list of changes: is → ______ ; has → ______ ; can → ______.
4) Write the direct speech for sentence a): He said, “______.”

After football training, the players talked to their coach.
Karim said, “I am tired.”
Salma said, “I am very thirsty.”
The boys said, “We are hungry.”

1) Report Karim's words. Begin with: He said (that) ...
2) Report Salma's words and the boys' words.
3) Which two things change in the reported sentences: the pronoun, the verb tense, the adjective?
4) Complete: with a past reporting verb, am and is change to ______, and are changes to ______.
Which pronoun changes in: She said, "I am here."

A journalist asked a family about their favourite drinks.
Mrs Ayari said, “I like coffee.”
Her son said, “I drink milk every morning.”
Her daughters said, “We don't like tea.”

1) Report Mrs Ayari's words. Begin with: She said (that) ...
2) Report her son's words and her daughters' words.
3) Complete the rule: present simple → ______ simple; don't → ______.
Report: "can" becomes ___.
Report a question: He asked, "Where do you live?"

Look at the table of time changes, then read the two sentences.
| Direct speech | Reported speech |
|---|---|
| now | then |
| today | ______ |
| tomorrow | the next day |

The teacher said, “We have a test today.”
Rim said, “I will finish my project tomorrow.”

1) Complete the table: how does today change in reported speech?
2) Report the teacher's sentence.
3) Report Rim's sentence.
4) Why do we change these time words?
